units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Nahum 3:15">Targ. Nah. III, 15</cite> (h. text <cite ref="J00400"><he>ילק</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 8:4">Eduy. VIII, 4</cite>, a. e. <he>איל ק׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A01264"><he>אַיִל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 77b:9">Sabb. 77ᵇ</cite> <he>מ״ט קרנא דק׳ וכ׳</he> why is the proboscis of the locust soft (flexible)?; [Rashi: = <cite ref="N00882"><he>נמלה</he></cite>, v. infra; early ed. Rashi: <cite ref="U00141"><he>שבלול</he></cite>].
<cite ref="Shabbat 77b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>האי מאן … לק׳ וכ׳</he> if you want to make a locust blind, break off its proboscis.

<cite ref="Yevamot 121b:12">Yeb. 121ᵇ</cite> <he>ודילמא ק׳ בעלמא וכ׳</he> perhaps it was merely a dead locust (or ant) to which playing children gave a man’s name?; a. fr.—Pl. <he>קַמְצִין</he>, <he>קַמְצֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 30:27">Targ. Prov. XXX, 27</cite> (h. text <cite ref="A02956"><he>ארבה</he></cite>); a. e.—

<cite ref="Taanit 21b:9">Taan. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>אמרו … אתו ק׳ וכ׳</he> when they told R. J. that the locusts were coming, he ordered a fast; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 5:4:6">Y. Ab. Zar. V, 44ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>אכל קמצין</he>, prob. to be read: <he>חמיצן</he>, v. <cite ref="H01214"><he>חָמֵץ</he> II</cite>.]

senses.gloss: (קְמַץ 1) [scraper, collector,] ant. Sabb. l. c.; Yeb. l. c., v. supra.—Pl. as ab.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 54b:4">Ber. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>אייתי … ק׳ וכ׳</he> the Lord sent ants which made holes in the mountain &c.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 21:5">Gen. R. s. 21</cite> <he>כהדין ק׳ דלבושיה וכ׳</he> (‘Rashi’ <cite ref="S00402"><he>קומצא</he></cite>) like the snail whose garment is part of its body. [The entire phrase is a gloss, v.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 34">Yalk. Gen. 34</cite>, and <cite ref="S01486"><he>קמצא</he></cite> is perhaps a clerical error for <he>לימצ״א</he> q. v.]
